notSaved: That didn't work. Please try again in a moment

general.startTip: This folder opens in the left panel after you sign in.
general.dblclickTip: A double click on a folder always opens it.
general.confirmTip: Shows everything that goes before it is deleted.
general.trashTip: Deleted things land in the bin first and can be brought back from there. Without the bin they are gone at once.
general.keepTip: After that the bin empties itself.
general.jobModeTip: One after another is kind to the disks: one job runs, the others wait in the order of the list. At the same time shares the bandwidth among all of them.
general.speedCapTip: All running jobs share this speed, so streams and downloads stay smooth. You slow down a single job in the jobs window.
general.parityWaitTip: Big copies from 2 GB wait until Unraid is done with the check or a rebuild. For small ones CannonCommander asks first. Both would share the same disks otherwise.
general.notifyDone: Tell me in the browser when done
general.notifyDoneTip: When a long job ends or fails, the browser shows a notification, also while the tab is in the background.
general.notifyUnraidTip: Also sends the notice to the notifications in the Unraid interface.
general.notifyAfterTip: CannonCommander does not report short jobs, you still see them running.
general.testBody: This is how the notice looks when a job is done
general.testBoth: Test notice sent to the browser and to Unraid
general.unraidFailed: Unraid did not take the notice. Is writing to Unraid switched on in the template?
general.notesBlocked: The browser does not allow notifications. You can allow them in the site settings of the browser

look.themeTip: System follows the setting of your device.
look.cornersTip: How round cards, buttons and windows are.
look.motionTip: How lively windows and pages come in. If your system asks for less motion, that always wins.
look.quietTip: Only shows errors and notes you can act on. Routine messages such as “Copied” stay away.
look.orderTip: Drag the tiles on the left to another place with the mouse.
look.buttonsTip: How much of a control is shown: its words, its symbol or both. Reactive shows only the symbol and brings in the words as soon as you point at it.
look.tabsTip: The settings tiles and every selector.
look.accentDimTip: Rainbow mode is on. Turn it off to pick an accent colour again.
look.accentReset: Reset the accent colour and the presets
look.rainbowTip: Every row in a list gets a colour of its own from a fixed set of eight, instead of everything wearing the same accent. Long lists become easier to tell apart at a glance.
look.discoTip: Every coloured row and element glides slowly on to the next colour of the palette while rainbow mode is on.
look.reactiveTip: When on, coloured rows and elements stay neutral until you touch them with the mouse or they are running or selected. So the colour only shows when it is needed. When off, every coloured row and element shows its colour all the time.
look.rotateTip: Shifts which palette colour counts as position 0, so the same list does not start with exactly the same colour every time rainbow mode comes on or the page reloads.

list.hiddenTip: Files whose name starts with a dot, such as .DS_Store. Ctrl+H switches them in the list too.
list.sizesTip: Adds up everything in a folder. Without the switch the list only says how many items it holds.
list.foldersFirstTip: Folders stand above the files, whatever the list is sorted by.
list.columnsTip: Columns can also be moved right in the column head, and a right click on the head shows or hides them.
list.sideTip: Shortcuts and the folder tree left of the panels.
list.fkeysTip: The buttons for F3 to F8 along the bottom, as in Total Commander.
list.quickviewTip: Shows a preview of the file under the cursor in the second panel. Turns on both panels for it.
list.liveTip: When other programs change files in the open folder, such as a download client, they show up without reloading and glow for a moment. While a window is open or something is marked, the list waits until you are done.

sources.title: Sources
sources.removeText1: {name} disappears from CannonCommander, along with its index.
sources.removeText2: The files in {path} stay on the server as they are.
sources.readOnlyTip: Nobody can change, delete or upload anything here, admins included.
sources.everyTip: CannonCommander reads folders where much changes more often and quiet ones less often, between 5 minutes and 12 hours. That keeps the search current, also when other containers change files.
sources.devicesTip: Unraid reports these. Admins see them below /mnt without adding them here. They are never indexed, so a sleeping disk stays asleep.
sources.name: Name
sources.pathTaken: This folder is a source already
sources.indexItTip: The index makes search and folder sizes fast. Reading in runs as a job in the background.
sources.skipHiddenTip: Files and folders whose name starts with a dot stay out of the index.
sources.excludeTip: One pattern per line: a name such as cache, a name with a star at its start or end such as *.tmp, or a path in the source such as appdata/plex/cache.
sources.readingAll: Every source is being read again
sources.planTip: Reads this again {every} right now, more often when much changes and less often when it stays quiet.
sources.restartTip: Changed sources count once CannonCommander starts again.
sources.savedRestart: Saved. It counts after a restart
sources.patternAll: This pattern matches everything. Better switch indexing off altogether
sources.patternPath: A path takes no star. Use a name such as *.tmp or a path such as appdata/plex/cache
sources.patternStar: A star works only at the start or the end of a name, such as *.tmp or backup-*

remotes.title: Remotes
remotes.removeText1: {name} is unmounted and forgotten, along with its credentials.
remotes.removeText2: The files at {type} stay where they are.
remotes.automountTip: Mounts every remote as soon as the container starts.
remotes.cacheTip: rclone keeps files here for a moment so programs can open them like local files. Full is fastest and takes the most space.
remotes.noType: Nothing found. SFTP and WebDAV fit almost any server.
remotes.endpointTip: Only needed when it isn't AWS.
remotes.folderTip: Leave empty for everything. Otherwise only this folder, such as /Photos.
remotes.accountTip: CannonCommander only gets a token, never your password.
remotes.onYourPcTip: On a computer with a browser and rclone. The command opens the sign in and then prints a token in the console.
remotes.tokenPh: Paste the token from the console here
remotes.needToken: Paste the token from the console first
remotes.tokenRejected: Signing in doesn't work with this token
remotes.name: Name
remotes.nameTip: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. rclone knows the remote by this name.
remotes.mountAtTip: The files show up under this folder in the file manager.
remotes.underRemotes: The folder has to be under /remotes, such as /remotes/{name}
remotes.testFailed: The connection doesn't work like this yet
remotes.savedNotMounted: {name} is saved, but mounting did not work

users.lastAdmin: There has to be at least one admin
users.removeText: {full} can't sign in any more after this.
users.removeTextShares: {full} can't sign in any more after this, and {shares} of {name} end.
users.filesStay: The files stay where they are.
users.removeGroupText: The group {name} and its access rules disappear.
users.savedPw: Saved, the new password works from now on
users.loginNameTip: Lowercase letters, the person signs in with it.
users.roleTip: Admins may do everything, here in the settings too. Users work with the files in their area. Read only can look and download.
users.scopeTip: The person only sees this folder and everything in it.
users.ownPwTip: You change your own password under Account and security.
users.newPwTip: A new password signs the user out everywhere.
users.nameRule: The sign-in name needs lowercase letters, at least two characters
users.needName: The sign-in name is still missing
users.nameTaken: That sign-in name is taken already
users.ownAdmin: Only another admin can take your own admin role
users.needAdmin: There has to be at least one admin
users.pwShort: The password needs at least 12 characters
users.pwDiffer: The two passwords aren't the same

access.title: Access for {who}
access.waysTip: Sessions, API tokens and passkeys. End them one by one or all at once.
access.noSessions: Not signed in anywhere right now
access.removePasskeyText: {who} can no longer sign in with {name}.
access.endAllText: {who} gets signed out everywhere, and every API token and passkey stops working.
access.passwordStays: The password stays as it is.
access.revokeTip: The new password signs the person out everywhere anyway. This also takes away their API tokens and passkeys.
access.savedPwEnded: Saved, the new password works and all access has ended

rules.title: Rules
rules.none: No rules, everybody sees their whole area
rules.up: Up, the first rule that fits wins
rules.resultTip: What this person sees at this path, after their area, their role and the rules.
rules.missingWhy: There is no such path on the server.
rules.noneReadonly: No rule fits, the role only allows reading.
rules.noneScope: No rule fits, the area applies.
rules.pathTip: A path applies to the folder and everything in it, and the folder above it can then not be deleted or moved. A pattern with a star fits names anywhere, such as *.partial*. Such files go along when their folder is deleted or moved, and copying leaves them out. A pattern with a slash, such as appdata/*/cache, works like a path.
rules.ruleTip: Allow lifts a rule further down, for a subfolder for example. The first rule that fits wins.
rules.needPath: The path or pattern is still missing
rules.noPath: There is no such path. For a pattern use a star, such as *.tmp
rules.readOnlySource: The whole source is set to read only.

shares.title: Shares
shares.none: No shares. You can share through File, Share.
shares.revoked: The link to {name} no longer works
shares.askPwTip: Whoever opens the link has to enter the password first.
shares.pwShort: The password needs at least 6 characters
shares.messageTip: Shown on the link's page above the files, such as a greeting or a hint. You can leave it empty.
shares.messagePlaceholder: such as: Here are the photos from the weekend

security.pwTip: A new password signs you out on every other device. This session stays signed in.
security.stayTip: After that CannonCommander asks for the password again.
security.onTip: After the password CannonCommander asks for a code from your app.
security.offTip: After the password CannonCommander also asks for a code from an app on your phone.
security.codesTip: Each code signs you in once if your phone is missing. New codes make the old ones invalid.
security.codesNew: The new codes work, the old ones no longer do
security.totpIsOff: Two-factor authentication is off. The password alone signs you in now
security.scanTip: Any app for one-time codes works, such as Aegis, 2FAS, Google Authenticator or your password manager.
security.appCodeTip: A code from the app or one of your recovery codes.
security.sixDigitsTip: The six digits the app shows right now. They change every 30 seconds.
security.sixDigits: Enter the six digits from the app
security.codeClock: The code doesn't fit. Is the time on your phone right?
security.needCode: Enter a code from the app
security.codesOnce: You only see these eight codes now. Keep them somewhere safe, in your password manager for example.
security.codesUse: If your phone is ever missing, each code signs you in exactly once.
security.newPwTip: At least 12 characters. A new password signs you out on every other device, this session stays signed in.
security.needCurrent: The current password is still missing
security.newShort: The new password needs at least 12 characters
security.sameAsOld: The new password is the same as the old one
security.newDiffer: The two new passwords aren't the same

pwChangedOthers.one: Password changed, one other device is signed out
pwChangedOthers.other: Password changed, {n} other devices are signed out

security.removePasskeyText: {name} won't sign you in after this. The password keeps working.
security.passkeyTip: Only works at {origin}. The password keeps working beside it.
security.passkeyNameTip: So you recognise the passkey in the list.
security.confirmPasskey: Confirm the passkey in your browser's window
security.passkeyFailed: The browser didn't create the passkey
security.allSignedOut: All other devices are signed out

signOut.one: One other device has to sign in again. This session stays.
signOut.other: {n} other devices have to sign in again. This session stays.

security.tokensStay: API tokens keep working, revoke them one by one below.
security.noToken: No token yet. Scripts and other programs sign in with one.
security.revokeText: Whatever uses {name} won't get in after this.
security.rightsTip: The token may never do more than you.
security.tokenNameTip: What the token is for. It shows up later in the list of tokens.
security.copyNow: Copy the token now. CannonCommander never shows it again, you can only create a new one.
security.pwLocked: Only an admin changes your password here, or you sign in through another service.
security.passkeysOff: Passkeys are switched off on this server
security.tooMany: Too many tries. Please try again in 15 minutes
security.proofTip: CannonCommander asks for it before every new way in, so only you can add one.
security.staleToken: A new token needs a fresh sign-in. This window opens again right after.
security.stalePasskey: A new passkey needs a fresh sign-in. This window opens again right after.

integrations.officeKindTip: Word, Excel and PowerPoint files then open for editing in the browser, in the quick look and with F3. Without a server CannonCommander shows them in its built-in preview.
integrations.urlTip: The address your office server answers at in the browser.
integrations.secretTip: Found in the office container's configuration as JWT_SECRET. Without it the server turns every file away.
integrations.badUrl: The address starts with http:// or https://
integrations.wantsSecret: The server answers but wants the JWT secret
integrations.unreachable: No office server answers at this address
integrations.thumbsTip: Small pictures for photos and videos in the preview. ffmpeg makes them in the background.
integrations.videoTip: Formats like MKV too. ffmpeg converts them while they play, which takes computing time.
integrations.webdavTip: Lets you mount the files as a drive, in Windows Explorer or a phone app for example. The same users and rules apply.
integrations.terminalTip: Admins can open a shell in the folder they are looking at, also by typing cmd or bash into the path row. It runs in the container with the rights of CannonCommander. Whoever opens it can do anything on the server that CannonCommander may do.
integrations.rcloneTip: Mounts the remotes. The program comes with the container.
integrations.secretWrong: The server turns this JWT secret down
integrations.notWorking: The server answers, but the connection does not work yet
integrations.alHint: ArrowLoop plans recurring syncs. CannonCommander hands it pairs of folders from the folder comparison.
integrations.alUrlTip: The address ArrowLoop has in the browser.
integrations.alTokenTip: A token from the ArrowLoop settings. With it CannonCommander may add jobs there.
integrations.alPathsTip: ArrowLoop often sees the shares under other paths, such as /data instead of /mnt/user. The path here goes on the left, the same folder in ArrowLoop on the right.
integrations.alUnreachable: No ArrowLoop answers at this address
integrations.alWantsToken: ArrowLoop answers, but wants a token

app.autoCheckTip: Once a day. You install an update yourself, on Unraid in the Docker tab.
app.tagTip: This version runs right now. Which tag Unraid pulls is set in the template, latest follows every new version.
app.toFileTip: All settings as a JSON file on the server, without passwords.
app.fromFileTip: Replaces the settings here with the ones from the file.
app.logTip: How much CannonCommander writes to the container log. On Unraid: Docker tab, CannonCommander, Logs.
app.restartText: CannonCommander is out of reach for a few seconds and reloads the page afterwards.

restartJobs.one: One running job stops with it.

app.exportDirTip: The server writes the file here, not into your browser's downloads.
app.secretsTip: Passwords, tokens, passkeys and the credentials of the remotes never go into the file.
app.takeUsers: Take over users, groups and rules
app.takeUsersTip: Passwords, passkeys and tokens stay here as they are.
app.notExport: That isn't an exported settings file
app.noAnswer: GitHub did not answer just now. Please try again later
app.restartNeededTip: A few settings count only after a restart.
app.importedRestart: {name} is taken over. Restart CannonCommander so all of it counts

info.versionHint: A click on a version number opens its release page.
info.glimstoneTip: The design language CannonCommander is built in
info.helpHint: For a bug report you download a file with the settings and the state of the jobs, without passwords, keys and credentials. Attach it to an issue on GitHub so it shows what happened on your server.
info.helpText: Problems, wishes or ideas for something better? Feel free to open an issue on GitHub, or send an email.
info.about1: One knight, one campaign: good-looking open source tools that didn't exist in the shape I wanted, built until nothing is missing. All free, no accounts, no telemetry, no ads, no paid tiers. No asterisk anywhere. Nothing readable ever leaves your own walls. Forged on evenings and weekends, with heart and a stubborn head.
info.about2: If CannonCommander has earned its place on your server, toss your knight a coin. It helps cover the costs and keeps the project alive. And it makes this knight's heart beat a little faster. Three ways are below, take the one that suits you.
info.coffee1: Toss your knight a coin: it covers part of the costs and keeps the project alive. Everything I build is free and shows no ads.
info.coffee2: Buy Me a Coffee takes cards, PayPal, Apple Pay and Google Pay. You don't need an account there.
info.paypalText: PayPal opens in a window of its own. With a card it works without a PayPal account too.
info.xrpNote: No destination tag and no memo needed.

news.title: New in {v}
news.intro: The first version: CannonCommander as a two-panel file manager for Unraid, with everything a server with several people needs.
news.files: Two panels with tabs, a folder tree and function keys
news.look: Theme, accent colour, corners and row height to your taste
news.users: Users & groups: everybody with a role and an area of their own
news.rules: Access rules and a probe of who sees what
news.remotes: Remotes through rclone, from SFTP to Google Drive
news.shares: Shares with an expiry date and a password
news.security: Two-factor authentication, passkeys and API tokens
news.activity: Activity: who did what and when

panels.title: Two panels
panels.text: Each side shows a folder. Tab switches between them, F5 copies what is marked to the other panel and F6 moves it. Ctrl+1 and Ctrl+2 switch between one and two panels.

mark.title: Marking
mark.text: Insert marks a row and moves to the next one, the space bar shows the file large in the quick look. Ctrl+click adds single ones, Shift+click a whole range. With + you mark by pattern, such as every *.jpg.

find.title: Finding
find.text: A / opens the quick filter in the current folder. Alt+F7 searches the whole server, fast thanks to the index under Settings, Sources.

share.title: Sharing and remotes
share.text: File, Share gives you a link with an expiry date and, if you like, a password. Google Drive, a NAS or another server you mount under Settings, Remotes. After that they sit in the folder tree like any other folder.

rights.title: Who may do what
rights.text: Everybody has a role and an area they can't leave. Access rules hide single folders in it or make them read only. Under Account and security you turn on two-factor authentication.
